subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A biopsy of the upper esophagus is examined under the microscope.
question: Which epithelial lining is expected in the normal esophagus?

options.text: Simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells

explanation_correct: The normal esophagus is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which protects against abrasive food boluses. In Barrett esophagus, chronic GERD replaces this with nonciliated columnar epithelium containing goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia). The muscularis externa of the upper third is striated muscle, transitioning to smooth muscle in the middle and lower thirds. Recognizing the normal lining is the key to identifying metaplasia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells lines the stomach and intestines, not the normal esophagus, except in Barrett metaplasia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Transitional epithelium lines the urinary tract, not the esophagus.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium lines the respiratory tract.
explanation_incorrect.E: Simple squamous epithelium lines blood vessels and alveoli, not the esophagus.

educationalObjective: The esophagus is normally lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A gastric biopsy is examined. The pathologist points out two cell types within the gastric glands that have distinct staining properties.
question: Which of the following correctly describes the staining of parietal and chief cells?

options.text: Parietal cells are basophilic; chief cells are eosinophilic
Parietal cells are eosinophilic (pink); chief cells are basophilic
Both parietal and chief cells are basophilic
Both parietal and chief cells are eosinophilic
Parietal cells are basophilic; chief cells are neutral-staining

explanation_correct: In the gastric glands, parietal (oxyntic) cells stain eosinophilic (pink) and secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor. Chief cells stain basophilic and secrete pepsinogen. Autoimmune destruction of parietal cells leads to chronic gastritis and pernicious anemia. The contrasting staining is a classic histologic identifier for these two cell types.

explanation_incorrect.A: This reverses the staining; parietal cells are eosinophilic and chief cells are basophilic.
explanation_incorrect.C: Chief cells are basophilic, but parietal cells are eosinophilic rather than basophilic.
explanation_incorrect.D: Chief cells are basophilic, so the two cell types are not both eosinophilic.
explanation_incorrect.E: Parietal cells are eosinophilic rather than basophilic, and chief cells are basophilic.

educationalObjective: Parietal cells are eosinophilic; chief cells are basophilic in gastric glands.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A biopsy from the duodenum shows fingerlike projections lined by epithelium and mucosa-associated glands located in the submucosa that secrete bicarbonate.
question: Which of the following features is characteristic of the duodenum but not of the colon?

options.text: Abundant goblet cells and no villi

explanation_correct: The duodenum features villi and microvilli that increase absorptive surface area, along with Brunner glands, which are bicarbonate-secreting cells located in the submucosa that neutralize gastric acid. It also contains crypts of Lieberkühn and plicae circulares in the distal duodenum. The colon, by contrast, has crypts with abundant goblet cells but no villi. Recognizing Brunner glands is the key to identifying duodenum histologically.

explanation_incorrect.B: Abundant goblet cells with no villi are characteristic of the colon, not the duodenum.
explanation_incorrect.C: Peyer patches are characteristic of the ileum, not specific to the duodenum.
explanation_incorrect.D: Gastric glands are found in the stomach, not the duodenum.
explanation_incorrect.E: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium lines the esophagus, not the duodenum.

educationalObjective: The duodenum is distinguished by villi and submucosal Brunner glands (bicarbonate secretion); the colon lacks villi.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A researcher examines the crypts of Lieberkühn in the small intestine and notes that they contain stem cells that replenish the epithelium as well as specialized cells that secrete antimicrobial products.
question: Which products are secreted by Paneth cells located in these crypts?
explanation_correct: Paneth cells reside in the crypts of Lieberkühn and secrete antimicrobial products including defensins, lysozyme, and TNF. The crypts also contain stem cells that replace enterocytes and goblet cells. This innate immune function is especially important in the small intestine. Paneth cell products are a classic histological and immunologic association.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bicarbonate is secreted by Brunner glands and pancreatic duct cells, not Paneth cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor are secreted by gastric parietal cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pepsinogen comes from gastric chief cells and gastrin from G cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Secretin and cholecystokinin are hormones from S and I cells of the duodenum and jejunum.

educationalObjective: Paneth cells in the crypts of Lieberkühn secrete defensins, lysozyme, and TNF.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A biopsy from the terminal ileum shows lymphoid aggregates within the lamina propria and submucosa. A biopsy from the jejunum shows tall, prominent mucosal folds that give a feathered appearance on oral contrast imaging.
question: Which of the following pairs each finding with the correct intestinal segment?

options.text: Peyer patches — jejunum; tall prominent plicae circulares — ileum
Peyer patches — duodenum; tall prominent plicae circulares — colon
Peyer patches — ileum; tall prominent plicae circulares — jejunum
Peyer patches — colon; tall prominent plicae circulares — duodenum
Peyer patches — stomach; tall prominent plicae circulares — ileum

explanation_correct: Peyer patches are unencapsulated lymphoid aggregates found in the lamina propria and submucosa of the ileum. The jejunum has taller, more prominent and numerous plicae circulares compared with the ileum, producing a feathered appearance with oral contrast and increased surface area. The ileum also has the largest number of goblet cells in the small intestine and plicae circulares in its proximal portion. Distinguishing jejunum from ileum is a classic histology test point.

explanation_incorrect.A: This swaps the segments; Peyer patches are in the ileum, and tall plicae are in the jejunum.
explanation_incorrect.B: Peyer patches are not found in the duodenum, and the colon does not have plicae circulares.
explanation_incorrect.D: Peyer patches are not a colonic feature; the colon also lacks villi and plicae circulares.
explanation_incorrect.E: Peyer patches are not found in the stomach, and tall prominent plicae are a jejunal feature.

educationalObjective: Peyer patches characterize the ileum, while tall prominent plicae circulares characterize the jejunum.
